correctness.rationale: The scalar/variable normalization is bijective after choosing \(u_0,u_1\), with \((q-1)^2\) lifts. For each admissible \(a\), \(N_0=N_2+2N_3\) follows by counting roots over all \(t\). The ordered-root-triple conic gives \(3N_0\) except at the explicitly separated triple-root parameter. For odd characteristic \(p\ne3\), its nonzero levels contain \(q-1\) or \(q+1\) points according as \(q\equiv1\) or \(2\pmod3\), by split-factor or norm counting. The exceptional \(a=1/3\) is admissible only when \(q\equiv2\pmod3\), and then cubing permutes the field, forcing zero cubic irreducibles. In characteristic three the conic has exactly \(q\) points, so each admissible \(a\) contributes \(q/3\). Full summation proves the three formulas; root enumerations in eighteen finite fields are reproducible finite checks only.

value.rationale: The original paper singles out I2 for exact evaluation but derives only an I3 lower bound; the present full-length-three enumeration is the first natural unsolved parameter of that sequence of questions. Its separate q mod 3 and characteristic-three regimes, together with the vanishing exceptional cubic fiber at a=1/3, encode real arithmetic structure, providing an exact benchmark for later length-four and maximal-length studies. It is not an arbitrary coefficient slice: all nonzero coefficient choices are counted.
